resources.title: Phonological Awareness
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Auditory perception and discrimination - Sounds of domestic animals such as cat, horse, dog, cock, cow, goat, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify and name sounds made by various animals; and 2. reproduce sounds made by animals.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Identifies the sounds of various animals. 2. Asks pupils to imitate the sound of the various animals.

Students: 1. Identify the sounds of the various animals as listed by the teacher. 2. Try to produce the various sounds.
resources.resources: 1. Picture books. 2. Pictures of animals. 3. Appropriate rhymes. 5. Teacher‘s demonstratio n.
resources.assessment: Pupils to : 1. name various sounds that animals make; and 2. mimic sounds made by animals.

resources.title: Phonemic Awareness #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Sounds of letters: - Production of basic sounds in given words correctly, e.g. /a,/b/,/d/
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. produce and identify basic sounds correctly; 2. distinguish the sounds of the different letters of the alphabet correctly; and 3. reproduce sounds of letters of the alphabet.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents and pronounces basic sounds correctly. 2. Presents and pronounces letters of the alphabet correctly. 3. Guides pupils to distinguish sounds of different alphabets correctly. 4. Guides pupils to pronounce the letters of the alphabet correctly.

Students: 1. Produce sounds and pronounce letters correctly. 2. Listen to teacher‘s pronunciation of letters of the alphabet. 3. Identify sounds of given alphabets. 4. Reproduce sounds of letters.
resources.resources: 1.Flash cards/Alphab et charts. 2.Toys 3. Pictures/ Drawing. 4. Real objects. 5. Tape recording / Sound charts.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. pronounce sounds of the letters of the alphabet correctly; and 2. identify letters and sounds in given words.

resources.title: Phonemic Awareness #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Word Sounds and Syllables
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. listen to one- syllable words and recognises words that begin with same letter sounds; 2. recognise words that end with same letter sounds; 3. identify rhyming words; 4. identify beginning and end sounds; 5. blend sounds to form one- syllable words e.g. ex, to, my, do, etc.; and 6. segment one - syllable words into separate letter sounds.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses pictures to lead pupils to identify sounds heard at the beginning and ending of the words e.g. dog; cat; etc. 2. Guides pupils to: - identify and count the number of sounds in a syllable. - identify letter sounds at the beginning, middle and end of spoken words; - blend letter sounds to form words; and - segment words into lettersounds.

Students: 1. Take turns to identify sounds of letters in words; 2. Listen to sentences and clap to each syllable in a word (e.g. sis-ter; man-go; hap-py; etc.) syllables in speech. 3. Build new words by blending letter sounds. 4. Distinguish between sounds at the beginning, middle and end of words. 5. Play Listening games:- listen to poems, Rhymes etc .and clap each time they hear a word.
resources.resources: 1. Word Cards 2. Audio Tape 3. Tape Recorders 4. Listening Game
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify beginning and ending sounds in one syllable words; 2. clap to the number of syllables in words; 3. form three- letter words by blending letter sounds; and 4. recognise letter sounds at the beginning, middle and ending of one syllable words.

resources.title: Phonemic Awareness #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Songs and Rhymes
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. sing songs taught; 2. recite rhymes; 3. identify letter sounds in songs and rhymes; 4. recognise rhyming words from given word sets; and 5. build rhyming word families.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Sings songs and recites rhymes with the pupils. 2. Guides the pupils to repeat sounds of rhyming words in the songs and rhymes. 3. Writes down sets of words on the board and lead pupils to identify word sets that rhyme. 4. Uses Pocket Chart to help pupils build rhyming word families.

Students: 1. Sing songs and recite rhymes after the teacher. 2. Reproduce sounds of rhyming words in songs and rhymes. 3. Match rhyming words to given word. 4. Build families of words that rhyme.
resources.resources: 1.Charts 2.Picture books with rhymes and songs 3.Flash cards 4.Tape recorder
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. recite rhymes and sing songs; 2. make the letter sounds in rhymes and songs; 3. Match rhyming words to given word;and 4. form new rhyming word sets.

resources.title: Phonics #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: The Alphabet: - Sounds of letters of the alphabet /a/ - /3/ - Names of all uppercase and lower case letters of the alphabet. - Alphabetical Order.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. say the sounds of the alphabet correctly; 2. recognise sounds of different letters of the alphabet; 3. describe the shapes of letters of the Alphabet; and 4. arrange the letters of the alphabet in the correct order.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Says the sounds of the alphabets. 2. Guides pupils to say the sounds of the alphabets.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher say the sounds of the alphabets. 2. Participate in saying the sounds of the letters of the alphabets.
resources.resources: 1. Cut – out letters of the alphabet. 2. Sounds chart. 3. Flash cards.
resources.assessment: Pupils to recognise and say sounds of the letters correctly.

resources.title: Phonics #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Blending sounds of Letters to form words e.g. /v/ -an (to form Van; or /c/ -an (to form Can); or /c/ -at (to form Cat); etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. build words by blending the sounds of letters of the alphabets.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Prepare Pocket Charts. 2. Makes sounds of letters of the alphabet for pupils to imitate. 3. Guides pupils to blend the sounds of letters to form words e.g. /v/ -an (to form Van; or /c/ -an (to form Can); or /c/ -at (to form Cat); etc. 4. Guides and directs drill exercises on blending sounds of letters to make new words.

Students: 1. Imitate sounds of letters. 2. Participate in class drills and exercises. 3. Build new words by blending sounds of the alphabets.
resources.resources: 1. Pocket Chart 2. Picture cards 3. Letter Cards 4. Word Charts
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. pronounce the sounds of the alphabets correctly; 2. blend the sounds to build three letter words; and 3. build sounds of the alphabets to build at least five new, but simple, words.

resources.title: Phonics #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1. Identification of familiar sounds in words e.g. house/mouse; try/fry; cat/bat/hat; etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read familiar words and text; 2. compare words with similar sounds; 3. apply long and short vowel rule correctly; 4. decode one-syllable word; and 3. monitor own reading and self corrects.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to track familiar sounds: - from words read aloud; - when reading own writing; and - in spoken words. 2. Provides pupils with appropriate drills and exercises to improve their reading.

Students: 1. Track sounds in spoken words in texts read. 2. Participate in reading drills and activities and self corrects own reading. 3. Read assigned books and stories.
resources.resources: 1. Pocket Chart 2. Picture cards 3. Letter Cards 4. Word Charts
resources.assessment: Pupils to 1. track familiar sounds in words; 2. identify sounds when re-reading own writing; and 3. read and self- correct own reading.

resources.title: Phonics #4
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 3. Decoding Strategies: - Sounding out words in text - Break words into smaller words - Words parts (compound words, digraphs) - Apply long and short vowels
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. break words into sounds; 2. break words into smaller words; 3. break words into parts and identify the word parts; 4. use letter-sound correspondence to build and read unfamiliar words; and 5. recognise and use vowel diagraphs and r-controlled letter sounds to read unfamiliar words .
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to: - Readwords placed in a row (e.g. doll – dot - dill and match text to the words). 2. Teaches correct pronunciation of words syllable by syllable while clapping and counting syllables in words; 3. Guides pupils to separate words into consonant and vowel sounds / parts. 4. Build words by blending word parts (long vowels/short vowels/ diagraphs, etc.) to form new words.

Students: 1. Match pictures to words read aloud. 2. Listen and clap to syllables in words. 3. Use pronunciation and listening games to: - recognise words from sounds - identify word parts; - Break words into small parts, - build and read unfamiliar words 4. identify, read and build compound words.
resources.resources: 1. Pocket Charts 2. Listening Games 3. Tape Recorders 4. Audio Tapes 5. Flash Cards 6. Word walls
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. sound out words they listen to; 2. identify smaller word in compound words; 3. identify the word parts in speech, words read aloud, etc.; and 4. build and read compound words and contractions.

resources.title: Fluency #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1. Reading Aloud with: - Pacing, - Intonation - Punctuations ; 2. Reading Variety of texts (poems, fantasy, etc.). 3. Independent Reading.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. correctly read letters of the alphabets; 2. read given text with fluency; and expression; 3. reflect appropriate pacing, intonation, punctuation when reading orally; 4. sight-read about 100-300 easily sounded words; and 5. read accurately without hesitations, omissions, repetitions, or mispronunciations .
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Prepare Pocket Charts. 2. Makes sounds of letters of the alphabet for pupils to imitate. 3. Guides pupils to the letters of the Alphabet fluently with in the correct order. 4. Helps pupils reflect pacing, punctuation and correct intonation while reading given text. 5. Gives class appropriate reading assignments to pupils to build speed and vocabulary.

Students: 1. Imitate sounds of letters. 2. Participate in class drills and exercises on reading. 3. Read a variety of texts (story books, newspapers, etc.). 4. Identifies and practice correct pronunciation of new words.
resources.resources: 1. Pocket Chart 2. Picture cards 3. Letter Cards 4. Word Charts 5. Story books 6. News Papers 7. Magazines 8. Charts 9. Content Specific Texts.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read the alphabets in the correct order without hesitation; 2. pronounce the sounds of the alphabets correctly; 3. recognise and express appropriate pacing, punctuations and intonation in reading; and 4. sight-read high frequency words in texts.

resources.title: Fluency #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Recognition of common 0ne- letter words (e.g. ―a‖; and ―I‖); two-letter (e.g. ―is‖, ―my‖); and three-letter words (e.g. ―the‖, ―was‖; ―can‖).
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. recognise common words (e.g. my, you, I, are, is, yes, no, etc.) by sight; 2. read class appropriate texts and sentences accurately without hesitation; and 3. use decoding to identify new words in reading passages.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes common 0ne-letter (e.g.‖a‖; and ―I‖); two-letter (e.g. ‖is‖, ―my‖;); and three-letter (e.g. ―the‖, ―was‖) words on the board. 2. Guides the pupils to: - correctly pronounce the words; - identify the words as letters of the alphabet; and - use the words in oral context in own speech. 3. Guides and directs oral drill reading exercises.

Students: 1. Pronounce given words correctly. 2. Use words in own speech. 3. Participate in drill exercises involving sight- reading of simple words and sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Pupil textbooks 2. Story books. 3. School Library.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. sight-read common one-letter, two-letter and three- letter words correctly; 2. use words in own speech; and 3. sight- read simple sentences accurately without hesitation.

resources.title: Comprehension #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Listening Comprehension: - Answering questions from stories. - Making connections and responding to story themes, plots and settings.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify main characters and setting of a story; 2. correctly answer questions about texts or stories read aloud, 3. explain sequence of events in stories (3-4) and indicate first, second, last, etc; and 4. re-tell and dramatises stories and parts of stories.
resources.activities:
Teacher: Reads a story to the class and guides pupils to: 1. identify characters in the story; 2. explain sequence of events; 3. make connections between story themes and characters in the story e.g. problems encountered, how the problems were solved, lessons learnt, etc; and 4. re-tell and dramatise parts of the story.

Students: 1. Listen to story read by the teacher. 2. Identify characters and settings in a story. 3. Answer questions based on story. 4. Re-tell parts of the story. 5. Dramatise the story. 6. Draw pictures to depict parts of the story.
resources.resources: 1. Story books. 2. School Library.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. answer questions based on stories read to them; 2. describe sequence of events in a story; 3. retell the story; 4. dramatise parts of a story; and 5. draw pictures that depict events in the story.

resources.title: Comprehension #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Written Comprehension: - Making connections and responding to story themes, plots and settings.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. describe information gained from texts in own words; 2. answer written comprehension questions based on materials read; 3. make predictions based on illustrations in stories or portions of stories; and 4. justify predictions of events in stories (draw a conclusion)
resources.activities:
Teacher: Guides pupils to read a text or story, and: 1. explain in own words the instructions and message in the text or story; 2. answer questions based on what is read; 3. make connections between story themes, characters in the story and life experiences; and 5. use pictures or portions of the story to make predictions and justify such predictions.

Students: 1. Read stories or texts from books. 2. Explain in own words instructions in texts or story. 3. Answer questions based on text or story. 4. Dramatise the story and connect information in story to life experiences. 5. Make predictions about events in the text or story.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils text books 2. Story books. 3. The School Library.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain in own words meaning of information in print texts; 2. correctly answer questions based on texts or stories read; 3. predict events based on illustrations in texts or stories; and 4. justify predictions with information from the text or story.

resources.title: Comprehension #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Reading informational text: - pictures, - illustrations, - Tables, - Charts, - Graphs, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain simple written instructions; 2. recognise main ideas drawn from looking at pictures, illustrations, tables, charts, graphs, etc.; 3. make predictions based on information contained in texts; and 4. justify predictions of events in stories (draw a conclusion)
resources.activities:
Teacher: Guides pupils to read and: 1. explain in own words the instructions and message in the text; 2. answer questions based on what is read; 3. Interprets to the class appropriate Charts, Graphs, Tables, etc.; 4. make predictions based on information contained in Tables, graphs, Charts, etc; and 5. justify such predictions.

Students: 1. Read and interpret given pictures, graphs, tables, charts, etc.. 2. Explain given instructions in own words. 3. Answer questions based on materials read. 4. Make and justify predictions about events based on contents of given Tables, Charts, Graphs, etc..
resources.resources: 1. Pupils Text books 2. Charts. 3. Graphs. 4. Tables
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. carry out simple instructions correctly; 2. interpret information contained in Pictures Tables, Charts, Graphs, etc.; 3. predict events based on illustrations in texts and other given materials; and 4. justify predictions with information from the text.

resources.title: Vocabulary Acquisition #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Reading Vocabulary Acquisition: 1. Word Categories: - Colours - Shapes - Foods - Animals, - Toys, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. name some basic words categories correctly; 2. sort pictures and words into basic word categories e.g. foods, colours, shapes, etc.; and 3. recognise and use abbreviations in simple sentences.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses pictures to lead pupils to: - identify word categories, and - groups words into the different categories. 2. Read stories to pupils and check their understanding by making them use key words in the story in a new sentence.

Students: 1. Match pictures to words read aloud. 2. Participates in Picture –Word matching game. 3. Identify word families and sort words into categories/ families. 4. Construct sentences using key words in the stories read.
resources.resources: 1. Story books. 2. Text books, 3. Picture books. 4. Word Cards. 5. Poems. 6. Dictionaries.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify word categories; 2. group words based on word categories correctly; and 3. use simple titles and abbreviations (Mr. Mrs. Dr. etc.) in sentences.

resources.title: Vocabulary Acquisition #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 3. Synonyms Antonyms, Homonyms
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the concept of synonyms and antonyms; 2. identify antonyms and synonyms correctly in own speech and in written texts and stories; and 3. identify homonyms.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to: 2. Identifies words with (a) similar meanings; and (b) opposite meanings; 3. Gives the synonyms and antonyms of common word; and 4. Identifies synonyms, antonyms and homonyms in stories.

Students: 1. Listen to the Teacher‘s explanations. 2. Take turns to give the synonyms and antonyms of common words. 3. Participate in drill exercises.
resources.resources: 1. Story books. 2. Text books. 3. Picture books. 4. Word Cards. 5. Poems. 6. Dictionaries.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the concept of synonyms and antonyms; and 2. identify antonyms and synonyms correctly in own speech and in written texts and stories.

resources.title: Concepts of Print #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1. Parts of a book: - Front Cover - Back Cover, - title, pages - Author, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Identify the front cover, back cover, Title, Author of a book, etc.; 2. identify upper and lowercase letters in printed words and sentences.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Reads a story to pupils. 2. Guides them to identify front cover, Back cover, Title and Author of the story book read.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the story. 2. Take turns to identify parts of the book i.e. front cover, title, title page, back cover, author, etc.
resources.resources: 1. Simple story books. 2. Pupils‘ text books. 3. School Library.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. name the parts of a book; and 2. identify contents of the different parts.

resources.title: Concepts of Print #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 3. Identification of Upper and Lower case Letters.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. name upper and lowercase letters in printed words and sentences; and 2. recognize and name upper and lower case letters in words and sentences.
resources.activities:
Teacher: Guides pupils to identify and name: - all upper case letters; and - lower case letters

Students: 1. Trace and letters in sand trays. 2. Trace letters in writing books. 3. Identify upper and lower case letters correctly.
resources.resources: 1. Simple story books. 2. Pupils‘ text books. 3. School Library.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify upper case and lower case letters in words and sentences; and 2. match letters printed on cards to names of the upper case and lower case letters.

resources.title: Concepts of Print #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 5. Eye movement: - reading from left to right; - top to bottom, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify the beginning and end of written words and sentences; 2. recognise that sentences are read from the top to the bottom of the page 3. Recognize that books are read from the front (beginning) to the back (end)
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify: - first and last word on a page; and - where to begin reading of printed words on a page. 2. Writes the some familiar words on the board and guide the pupils to read and point at the words as they read from left to right.

Students: 1. Make correct eye movement and hold their reading materials correctly. 2. Listen to story read and identify words that start the story, end the story, etc. 3. Read and point to words.
resources.resources: 1. Word Charts. 2. Flash Cards. 3. Books and reading materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to read printed words correctly from left to right and from top to bottom.

resources.title: Sounds and Letters
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1. Production of basic sounds in given words correctly e.g. /a,/b/,/d/. 2. Correct pronunciation of letters of the alphabet e.g A, B, C.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. produce and identify basic sounds correctly; and 2. pronounce letters of the alphabet correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents and pronounces basic sounds correctly. 2. Guides pupils to pronounce and identify basic sounds correctly. 3. Presents and pronounces letters of the alphabet correctly. 4.Guides pupils to pronounce the letters of the alphabet correctly.

Students: 1. Produce sounds and pronounce letters correctly. 2. Identify sounds of given words. 3. Listen to the teacher‘s pronunciation of letters of the alphabet.
resources.resources: 1 .Flash cards/Alphabet charts. 2.Toys 3. Pictures/ Drawing. 4. Real objects. 5. Tape recording / Sound charts.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. pronounce sounds of the letters of the alphabet correctly; and 2. identify letters and sounds in given words.

resources.title: Songs and Rhymes
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1.Clear recitation of various rhymes depicting nature, care, kindness and love. 2. Short songs which appeal to children‘s sentiments.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. listen to songs and rhymes attentively; 2. sing songs taught; and 3.recite rhymes.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents a rhyme reads it aloud, pronouncing the words clearly. 2. Writes the rhyme on the chalk board and encourages pupils to recite the rhyme clearly. 3. Introduces song by singing it clearly and encourages pupils to sing the song.

Students: 1. Listen while teacher recites rhymes. 2. Recite rhymes after the teacher. 3. Recite rhymes alone sounding words clearly.
resources.resources: 1.Charts 2.Picture books with rhymes and songs 3.Flash cards 4.Tape recorder
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. listen to rhymes attentively; and 2. recite rhymes and sing songs with demonstration where appropriate.

resources.title: Simple greetings and Commands
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1.Greetings at home and appropriate time for particular greetings e.g: Pupil: ―Good morning dad, how do you do?‖ Dad: ―Good morning Ade, How do you do?‖ 2. Greetings at school e.g. Pupil: ‗‘Good morning Madam/Sir/Mr. Obi.‘‘ Teacher: ―Good morning Olu, how are you?‖ Pupil: ―I am very well thank you Sir.‖ 3. Greetings in the community, neighbours, elders/clan heads, nurse, doctor. e.g. ―Good afternoon‘ Doctor/ Sir/Madam etc. 4. Simple commands at home: e.g ‗wake-up!‘, ‗go to bed‘, ‗greet your daddy‘
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. greet and respond to simple greetings with appropriate tones; 2. give and carry out simple commands; and 3. differentiate between tones in greetings and commands.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Creates home and school atmosphere through role play characters e. g father, mother, elder, teacher, etc. 2. Demonstrates appropriate greeting for each character 3. Encourages pupils to greet one another with appropriate gestures 4. Gives commands and demands appropriate responses from pupils.

Students: 1. Role-play members of the family, home, school and class community. 2. Demonstrate appropriate greetings for different people. 3. Greet and respond to greetings from colleagues. 4.Obey the teacher‘s commands. 5. Model giving and obeying commands in pairs.
resources.resources: 1.Pictures depicting modes of greeting among various groups 2. Charts
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1.greet and respond to simple greetings; and 2.give and respond to commands using the appropriate tone.

resources.title: Identification of persons, objects, colours and animals.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1. Introductions, such as: ―What is your name?‖ ―My name is Tinu‖. ‗‘What is your father‘s/mother‘s/brother‘s /sister‘s name?‘‘ 2 .Identification of objects at home e.g. bed, mat, radio. ―What is this?‖ ―Show me a cup‖. Etc. 3. Identification of major colors: white, red, blue, yellow, black. 4.Description of things according to their colours. e.g ‗yellow bag‘, ‗red bucket‘. ―Give me the green book‖ etc. 5.Identification of animals - Domestic animals e.g ‖cats, dogs and goats‖ -Wild animals e.g. Lions, Elephants and Hyenas.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify self, family members e.g. father, mother brother and sister etc; 2. identify named objects: at home, on the way to and from school, and in the school compound; 3. identify primary colours associating them with objects appropriately; 4. identify named animals; and 5. clearly pronounce names of objects, persons, colours identified.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1.Introduces himself to the class ―My name is Abu‖. 2. Asks different pupils their names, names of family members. 3. Guides different pairs of children to introduce themselves to one another. 4. Presents different household, classroom, and school objects, and guides pupils to identify them by name, e.g a bag, a table. 5. Associates colours with objects in the classroom. 6. Guides pupils to identify objects of named colours.

Students: 1. Say their names and those of family and class members clearly. 2. Participate in self introduction. 3. Identify given objects by names and colours. 4. Explain what domestic and non- domestic animals are with examples.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures 2. Charts 3. Real objects 4. Brightly coloured picture books.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. introduce themselves; 2. identify persons by names; 3. identify major colours; and 4. name some domestic and wild animals.

resources.title: Expressing possession
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Using the possessives my, yours, his, hers, in simple correct sentences e.g.: a. This is my pen. b. This is your pen. c. This is his/her pen.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to use singular forms of possessives to express ownership.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains possessive forms: forms that show ownership. 2. Lists possessive words. 3. Uses possessives in sentences and encourages pupils to repeat his examples. 4. Asks pupils to make their own sentences.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher‘s explanation. 2. Repeat teacher‘s examples. 3. Make their own sentences using possessives in clear correct sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Real objects 2. Picture of objects 3. Course book.
resources.assessment: Pupils to : 1. name some possessives; and 2. use singular forms of possessives in simple correct sentences.

resources.title: Expressing gratitude and farewell.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: 1.Expressing gratitude through role play 2. Expressing farewell in various ways and situations. 3. Expressing farewell. .
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Express gratitude correctly. 2. Say farewell to people correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1.Leads pupils to mention occasions when we should express gratitude e.g. when we receive gifts, when people show us kindness or are polite to us. 2. Makes sentences expressing gratitude to children, parents, elders. 3. Asks pupils to repeat the sentences. 4. Guides children to role play a situation which allows them to express gratitude. 5. Makes sentences expressing farewell in various ways e.g. goodbye, farewell, bye-bye.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher and repeat the teacher‘s expression. 2. Dramatise different situations for using ―thank you‖, Ma/Sir/Daddy etc. e.g. after eating our food, when we receive gifts from people. 3. Role play ―farewell‖
resources.resources: 1. Pictures depicting relevant situations. 2. Wall charts 3. Course books 4. Audio/video tapes.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1.express gratitude to their peers correctly; 2. make sentences using thank you; and 3. say farewell, bye-bye, good bye to people correctly.

resources.title: Asking and Answering Questions
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 1 | Content: Simple questions and answers, such as: i. ‗What is your name?‘ ‗My name is Olu‘. ii. ‗What is your father‘s name?‘ ‗My father‘s name is Ahmed‘.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1.ask simple questions using ‗what‘; and 2. answer simple questions correctly
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1.Asks simple questions from pupils using ‗what‘. 2. Leads them to give correct answers to the questions. 3. Pairs pupils and guides them as they take turns to ask one another questions and answer them.

Teacher: 1. Presents class appropriate story and poem for pupils to read. 2. Leads pupils to read and retell what they have read 3. Explains the meaning of the poem to pupils, 4. Guides pupils to dramatize the story. 5. Leads pupils to identify the values and lessons in the stories and poems.

Students: 1. Participate in reading the story and poem. 2. Dramatize the poem. 3. Identify values and lessons in pairs or in groups.
resources.resources: 1. Poetry and story books 2. A flannel board containing the poem to be taught. 3. Pictures depicting values in the poem. 4. Posters 5. Flash cards.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read given simple stories and poems; and 2. identify values/ lessons learnt.

resources.title: Comprehension #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Oral Comprehension based on: (a) Stories - e.g. - stories built on any topic such as Road Safety, National Values, Disaster Risk Reduction, Dangers of Chemicals, Drug Abuse, HIV/AIDS etc; - stories that will encourage them to tell their own stories in simple English, e.g. ―The house that Jack built‖.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. listen carefully to a story; 2. answer questions on the main points in the story in their own words; and 3. re-tell the story in their own words.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tells a story slowly, stressing important points with the correct intonation. 2. Asks questions and gives pupils the opportunity to re-tell the story. 3. Guides and supervises pupils‘ activities.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher telling or reading the story. 2. Re-tell the story. 3. Answer questions on the story.
resources.resources: 1. Course book or Supplementar y Readers. 2. Relevant pictures or real objects.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. answer questions on the main points in the story; and 2. relate a story in their own words;

resources.title: Comprehension #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 2. Reading class appropriate passages (non- fiction) and answering questions on them e.g. - Simple passages based on national values e.g. discipline and courage; respect for elders etc. - Identification and use of new words in sentences - Identification and discussion of issues of national values in the passage.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read simple non-fiction passages correctly; 2. answer questions on the passages 3. explain the meaning of difficult words in the passage; and 3. identify and discuss issues of national values in a given passage.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to read a given passage silently individually or aloud in turns. 2. Asks questions and guides pupils to answer them. 3. Guides pupils to identify and explain the meaning of difficult words 4. Leads pupils to use new words in the passage in sentences. 5. Guides pupils to identify and discuss national values in the passage.

Students: 1. Read the passage silently to get the main ideas contained in it. 2. Read it again to get the details. 3. identify and explain the meaning of difficult words in the passage. 4. identify and discuss national values in the passage. 5. Answer the comprehensi on questions.
resources.resources: 1. Course book. 2. Simple passages from magazines and other relevant materials available to the pupils. 3. List of new words to learn from passage on flip chart or chalk board.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read given passages correctly; and 2. answer questions on the passage.

resources.title: Comprehension #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 3. Reading simple poems on: - discipline - courage - courtesy - road safety etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read simple poems; and 2. identify values and lessons in given poems.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents a relevant poem. 2. Guides pupils to read and dramatise the poem. 3. Explains the meaning of the poem to pupils. 4. Leads pupils to identify the values and lessons.

Students: 1. Participate in reading the poem. 2. Dramatise the poem. 3. Identify values and lessons in pairs or in groups.
resources.resources: 1. Poetry books 2. A flannel board containing the poem to be taught. 3. Pictures depicting values in the poem. 4. Posters 5. Flash cards
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read a given simple poem; and 2. identify values/less ons learnt.

resources.title: Comprehension #4
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 5. Reading charts, diagrams, graphs, calendars etc. to obtain information
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read information on charts, diagrams, calendars, etc.; 2. Obtain information from charts, diagrams and calendars.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Shows pupils relevant charts, graphs, diagrams, calendars etc. 2. Illustrates to pupils how information can be obtained from the above. 3. Asks questions and guides pupils to find answers to them from the charts, graphs, diagrams, calendars etc.

Students: 1. Observe charts, graphs, diagrams, calendars presented by teacher. 2. Answer teacher‘s questions individually, in pairs or in groups.
resources.resources: 1. Calendars. 2. Course book. 3. Relevant charts, diagrams, graphs.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read charts, diagrams, graphs, calendars etc 2. answer questions on charts, diagrams, graphs and calendars.

resources.title: Comprehension #5
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 7. Extensive/ independent Reading: - Reading selected stories and chapters from books
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read selected stories on their own. 2. retell the stories.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Teacher selects appropriate fictional materials and chapters from books for pupils to read. 2. Asks questions on the books read.

Students: 1. Pupils read selected material independently, 2. They answer questions on what they have read.
resources.resources: 1. Supplementary reading materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Read given materials correctly. 2. Answer questions on the materials correctly.

resources.title: Vocabulary
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: Vocabulary Acquisition: (a) Using poems on discipline, courage, courtesy, road safety etc. to expand children‘s vocabulary. (b) Substitution of words in poems. (c) Explanation of the relationship between words. (d) Development of new words.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. substitute words in poems 2. explain the relationship between words; and 3. develop new words.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents a class appropriate poem. 2. Guides pupils to read the poem. 3. Guides pupils to substitute words in the poems with appropriate words. 4. Explains relationship between words to pupils. 5. Guides pupils to develop new words.

Students: 1. Participate in reading the poem. 2. Read the poem. 3. Substitute words in the poems with appropriate words. 4. Explain the relationship between words 5.develop new words
resources.resources: 1. Poetry books 2. A flannel board containing the poem to be taught. 3. Pictures depicting values in the poem. 4. Posters 5. Flash cards.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read given simple poems 2. explain the relationship between words; and 3. substitute four words in the poem with others.

resources.title: Concepts of Print
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Recognition of title page, margins, illustrations, pictures, diagrams, labels, etc. in printed texts/materials.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. recognise that title page, illustrations, margins, pictures, diagrams are components of printed materials, etc 2. obtain information from charts, diagrams and calendars etc.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Shows pupils title page, illustrations, margins, picture, charts, graphs, diagrams, etc in texts. 2. Illustrates to pupils how information can be obtained from the above. 3. Asks questions and guides pupils to identify graphs, diagrams, pictures etc.

Students: 1. Observe, graphs, diagrams, labels etc in texts presented by teacher. 2. Answer teacher‘s questions individually, in pairs or in groups.
resources.resources: 1. Supplementa ry Readers 2. Course book. 3. Relevant charts, diagrams, graphs, Labels, Signs etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to identify diagrams, graphs, title page, illustrations, margins, pictures ,etc in texts etc

resources.title: Use of Capital Letters, Punctuation Marks – Full Stop, Comma, etc
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Various uses of capital letters/higher cases 2. Uses of full stop and comma. E.g. at the end of sentences and for listing a series of items respectively and for separating ideas or clauses in sentences.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. get an understanding that ‗capital letters‘ and ‗higher cases‘ mean the same thing 2. use capital letters/higher cases correctly; and 3. use the punctuation marks e.g. comma, semi-colon, exclamation marks, etc correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes sample sentences using higher cases, punctuation marks such as full stop, comma, colon, semi-colon, etc. 2. Explains various uses of comma. 3. Asks pupils to give similar examples 4. Asks them to write their own examples in their books.

Students: 1. Read the examples given by the teacher 2. Listen to teacher‘s explanation 3. Make similar sentences of their own 4. Write teacher‘s examples in their books 5. Do several exercises on the use of capital letters and punctuation marks.
resources.resources: 1. Selected passages from course book. 2. Sample sentences showing the various uses of capital/higher cases and the punctual marks.
resources.assessment: Pupils to use the capital letters/higher cases and punctuation marks correctly.

resources.title: Writing Three to Four Sentences on Everyday Activities using Present and Past Tenses
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 3 | Content: Writing three to four sentences on habitual activities using present and past tenses.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. use habitual sentences in both present and past tenses. Examples: - Present- 1. Audu dances well. 2. He eats amala very well - Past- 1. Audu danced yesterday. 2. He ate amala.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Teacher explains what habitual sentences mean. 2. He writes samples of habitual sentences in present tenses as well as in past tenses.

Students: 1. Pupils listen to the teacher‘s explanation 2. Write examples of habitual sentences in their book 3. They write similar sentences as homework.
resources.resources: 1. Charts on sample tenses 2. Work book. 3. Any other relevant materials
resources.assessment: Pupils to write habitual sentences correctly.

resources.title: Handwriting
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 3 | Content: Passages highlighting national values e.g. discipline, honesty and courage.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read simple passages on the content column; 2. copy the passage into their exercise books in their own handwriting; 3. write clearly and legibly; and 4. observe the spacing between letters in a word and words in a sentence.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Reads to give a model example. 2. Writes passage on the board. 3. Guides the pupils to identify some difficult words in the passage. 4. Shows them the spacing between letters in a word and words in a sentence. 5. Asks pupils to copy passage into their notebooks 6. Supervises and makes corrections where necessary.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s reading. 2. Read the passage following teacher‘s example. 3. Identify some difficult words in the passage. 4.Observe the spacing between letters in a word and words in a sentence. 5. Copy the passage into their writing exercise book. 6. Do corrections where necessary.
resources.resources: 1. Passages under content column. 2. Any other relevant reference materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read given passages correctly; and 2. copy correctly the given passage into their exercise books.

resources.title: Writing Answers to Questions on Simple Comprehension Passages
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Writing answers to comprehension passages from the course book, supplementary readers and any other structures 2. Identifying structural words and verb forms already dealt with. 3. Copying identified words and structures in legible handwriting.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. write answers to questions based on a passage 2. read simple passages effectively; 3. skim simple passages for main ideas; and 4. identify words and verbs already learnt.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents short comprehension passages and guides pupils to study the passages 2. Asks questions on them. 3. Tells pupils to write the answers in their exercise books.

Students: 1. Read the passages silently and quickly for the first time after teacher’s pattern reading and explanation. 2. Read it slowly the second time, noting the main points and details. 3. Answer questions on it orally. 4. Copy in their own handwriting on the chalkboard and into their exercise books.
resources.resources: 1. Course book. 2. Supplementary readers. 3. Any other relevant material.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. write answers to a few questions based on a passage they read; 2. skim given passage for general ideas; and 3. identify words and structures already learnt.

resources.title: Pronunciation of Consonants and Consonant Clusters
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Production of consonant sounds in isolation, words and in context 2. Pronunciation practice on consonant clusters e.g: /b/ bl - blade, /br/ - bread, /dr/ – dry /fr/ – frog, /f/ - flood, /g/ - grass, /k/ - clipper, quick, /pl/ please, /pr/ - price, /s/ slate, /sm/ smiles, /tr/ train, /st/ stone, /spr/ spread e.g i. This blade is very sharp. ii. I ate bread this morning. iii. Spread the clothes on the grass
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. pronounce consonants sounds in isolation, in words and in sentences correctly; 2. differentiate between words in each pair in isolation and in sentence context; and 3. produce consonant clusters correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes the words and the sounds on the board. 2. Demonstrates correct articulation of the sounds. 3. Asks pupils to repeat the sounds after him. 4. Corrects identified pupils‘ problems with the sounds

Students: 1. Watch the teacher write the sounds on the board. 2. Copy the articulation of the sounds into their books. 3. Pronounce the words after the teacher. 4. Practice the correct pronunciation of the words/sounds in sentence context. 5. Have more practice in pronouncing such words for the teacher to assess.
resources.resources: 1. 1. Objects. 2. Pictures of objects. 3. Flash cards. 4. Flannel board 5. Wall charts 6. Course book
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. pronounce consonants sounds in isolation, in words and in sentences correctly and 2. differentiate between sounds in pairs of words correctly.

resources.title: Making Simple Statements and Responding to Simple Commands with Emphasis on Stress and Intonation.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Making simple statements using the appropriate stress and intonation. 2. Responding to simple commands appropriately. .
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. make simple statements correctly with the appropriate stress and intonation; and 2. respond to simple commands appropriately.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Makes model statements with the appropriate stress and intonation. 2. Gives commands to pupils, paying attention to the correct stress and intonation. 3. Guides pupils in making statements and responding to commands.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s Statements and commands. 2. Repeat the statements after the teacher. 3. Follow teacher‘s commands appropriately.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Supplementary text. 3. Charts containing simple sentences.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. construct simple sentences with the appropriate stress and intonation; and 2. respond to given commands correctly.

resources.title: Simple Dialogues Expressing Present, past and Future Actions.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Simple dialogues – dialogues in present, past and future actions. 2. Asking and answering simple questions using present, past and future tenses with the appropriate intonation e.g i. Question: Where is the teacher? Answer: He is in the class. ii. Question: Who is Mallam Dikko? Answer: Mallam Dikko is the head teacher.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. participate in simple dialogues using present, past and future tenses. 2. ask and answer simple questions correctly using present, past and future tenses; and 3. practise the use of the rising and falling tunes in questions and answers correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains what dialogue is 2. Gives examples of dialogue shown in the content column. 3. Gets pupils to engage in dialogues in present, past and future tenses, ensuring that the correct stress and intonations are observed. 4. Guides pupils to practice the use of the rising and falling tones correctly.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher‘s explanation. 2. Repeat the dialogues after the teacher observing the correct stress and intonation (rising and falling tones). 3. Practice the dialogues in twos and in groups, both inside and outside the classroom.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Sentence strip. 3. A volunteer pupil for rehearsal. 4. Other suitable materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. ask two questions and answer them correctly through simple dialogues; and 2. engage in dialogues using the rising and falling tones.

resources.title: Oral Comprehension
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1 .A story that will interest the pupils but built on any topic such as Road Safety, National, Values, Disaster Risk Reduction, Drug Abuse, HIV/AIDS etc. 2. Provide stories that will encourage them to tell their own stories in simple English e.g the house that Jack built; 3. Prepare them for future life.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able t: 1. to listen carefully to a story; 2. answer questions on the main points in the story in their own words; 3. re-tell the story in their own words; and 4. tell similar stories.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tells the story slowly, stressing important points with the correct intonation 2. Asks questions 3. Gives pupils the opportunity to tell their own stories. 4. Guides and supervise pupils‘ activities.

resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. answer questions on the main points in the story; 2. relate story in their own words; and 3. participate in telling similar stories.

resources.title: Pronunciation of vowels and diphthongs.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Pronunciation practice: e.g a,e,i,u /i e / and / ea / here hare ear air fear fare/fair beer bear/bare e.g. the hare was here yesterday.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. produce vowel sounds and diphthongs correctly 2. distinguish between vowels and diphthongs by pronouncing them correctly in words and sentence contexts.

Teacher: 1. Demonstrates and pronounce the words or show objects or their pictures while repeating the words correctly. 2. Lets the pupils imitate him. 3. Engages pupils in drills, using the minimal pair 4. Dictates words to the pupils to copy.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher. 2. Produce the sounds used in each pair of words correctly. 3. Write dictation based on the use of these words.
resources.resources: 1. Relevant pictures of objects. 2. Flash cards 3. Flannel board. 4. Course book.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1.distinguish between the sound /id/ and / ed / by pronouncing them Correctly; 2. write correctly five words dictated by the teacher.

resources.title: Aural Discrimination
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 3 | Content: Aural discrimination of the sounds: i. / 3/ and / ^: / burn - born firm – form perch – porch - I can burn this bush. A new child is born - The firm sent a form to me ii. / D / and / Ɔ:/ cot – court spot – sport.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. pronounce and distinguish between the sounds in words and sentences using the correct stress and intonation; and 2. distinguish between the different sounds in words and sentences.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Reads the sentences containing the sounds 2. Distinguishes between the sounds. 3. Pronounces the words paying attention to the stress and intonation. 4. Asks pupils to repeat after him.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher‘s reading. 2. Repeat after teacher. 3. Distinguish between the sounds. 4. Pronounce the words. 5. Read the sentences following teacher‘s example.
resources.resources: 1. Flash cards. 2. Sentence strips. 3. Flannel board. 4. Course book.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. pronounce given words using the appropriate sounds; and 2. distinguish between the sounds in words and sentences using the correct stress and intonation.

resources.title: Use of Regular and Irregular Plurals in Speaking and Writing
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 3 | Content: 1. Regular plurals e.g. ball/balls; boy/boys. 2. Irregular plurals e.g. child/children; foot/feet
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify regular and irregular plurals 2. use regular and irregular plurals in simple sentences

Teacher: 1. Teacher presents the correct use of regular and irregular plurals in speeches. 2. The correct use of irregular and irregular plurals in writing.

Students: 1. identify regular and irregular plurals in speeches and writings. 2. to use regular and irregular plurals in speeches and writings.
resources.resources: 1. Real objects 2. Pictures of objects 3. Charts 4. Flash cards
resources.assessment: Pupils to : 1. identify regular and irregular plurals in speeches and writings; and 2. pupils to use regular and irregular plurals in speeches and writings.

resources.title: Use of Auxiliary Verbs

resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Teacher to present and demonstrate the correct use of auxiliary verbs in sentences. 2. Facilitates flash card games to aid pupils understanding of auxiliary verbs.

resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify auxiliary verbs in sentences; and 2. use auxiliary verbs in sentences

resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. make correct sentences in the simple future tense; and 2. respond correctly to interrogative sentences using contracted forms of ―will‖ and ―shall‖.

resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Supplementary materials 3. charts
resources.assessment: Pupils to : 1 .identify past continuous tense in sentences; and 2. use past continuous tense in sentences.

resources.assessment: Pupils to : 1. identify present perfect with ―since‖ and ―for‖; and 2. use ―since‖ and ―for‖ in sentence construction.

resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 3 | Content: Interrogation and Responses using present perfect e.g. Interrogation: Have you finished your home work? Response: No, I have not. Interrogation: Are you going to play football with me today? Response: Yes, of course.
